title: Limits of Stochastic Semigroups and Block-Triangular Majorisation
authors: Fabio Deelan Cunden, Jakub Czartowski, Giovanni Gramegna, Marilena Ligabò
abstract: We investigate limits of semigroups of stochastic matrices defined by their invariant distribution. Given probability vectors $γ(β)$ depending on a parameter $β$, we introduce a notion of convergence as $β\to\infty$ for the corresponding semigroups of $γ(β)$-preserving stochastic matrices and investigate the structure of the resulting limit. In general, the limiting semigroup differs from the semigroup preserving the limiting distribution, showing that these two operations do not commute. We develop a general framework for such limiting semigroups and study in detail the case in which the invariant distributions are Gibbs vectors at the inverse temperature $β$. We show that the limiting semigroup consists of block-upper-triangular stochastic matrices subject to additional substochasticity constraints. We characterise and enumerate their extremal elements and determine the preorder on probability vectors induced by the action of the semigroup. The resulting notion of Block-Triangular majorisation interpolates between ordinary majorisation and upper triangular (aka unordered) majorisation. We show that it is completely characterised by a finite family of monotones and analyse the corresponding behaviour of Rényi $α$-entropies as $β\to\infty$.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the limiting behavior of stochastic semigroups derived from Gibbs distributions as temperature approaches zero. It proves that the limit of the semigroups does not generally commute with taking the semigroup of the limit distribution. The resulting structure is characterized by block-upper-triangular matrices, defining a novel mathematical concept called Block-Triangular majorisation.
main_problem: The paper investigates the mathematical structure of the limit of stochastic semigroups associated with probability vectors $\gamma( eta)$ as the inverse temperature $ eta$ approaches infinity.
main_result: The limiting semigroup is generally not the semigroup preserving the limiting distribution, but rather a subsemigroup characterized by block-upper-triangular stochastic matrices, leading to a new concept called Block-Triangular majorisation.
method: The authors develop a general framework involving multiscale decomposition and analyzing the Kuratowski limit of the semigroups, utilizing majorization theory and combinatorial counting.
model_or_system: The model involves stochastic matrices whose invariant distributions are Gibbs vectors $\gamma( eta) \propto e^{- eta E_i}$, arising in the context of statistical mechanics at varying temperatures.
key_observables: Stochastic matrices, semigroups, Block-Triangular majorisation, and Rényi $\alpha$-entropies.
important_parameters: The inverse temperature $ eta$, particularly its limit $ eta 	o \infty$ (zero-temperature limit).
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on the exponential separation of scales in the Gibbs case and the existence of a limiting temperature $ eta_0$ for certain inequalities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the non-commutativity of limit operations using different asymptotic trajectories and provide flowcharts detailing the extreme points of the stochastic semigroups for small systems ($n=3, 4$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes a general framework for limiting semigroups, specializes this to the Gibbs case using multiscale profiles, characterizes the resulting block-upper-triangular structure, and proves the equivalence between this structure and the Block-Triangular majorisation preorder.
why_interesting: The non-commutativity result is crucial for understanding how thermodynamic limits affect the dynamics of open quantum systems, suggesting that the path taken to the limit matters significantly.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Dependence of the limiting distribution-preserving semigroup on the multi- scale profile. Two families of probability vectors, 𝛾(𝛽) and e𝛾(𝛽), converge to the same boundary point of Δ2 as 𝛽→∞, while approaching it along different asymptotic tra- jectories. Consequently, their associated semigroups of preserving stochastic matrices have different Kuratowski limits, illustrating that the limiting distribution alone does not determine the limiting semigroup. In particular, limiting semigroup in degenerate case (𝑥= 1, blue line) is different from non-degenerate cases (𝑥= 1.5, 2; magenta and red lines, respectively).
